t: In addition to the amounts otherwise provided by section 101, an additional amount is provided for “Department of the Interior—National Park Service—Operation of the National Park System” for security and visitor safety activities related to the Presidential Inaugural Ceremonies, at a rate for operations of $2,000,000.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriations provision that gives the National Park Service additional funding for inauguration security and visitor safety. The tempting reading is that "visitor safety" and public ceremonies bring the public in, but visitors are only beneficiaries of the spending and are not consulted on any federal decision. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, outside consultation, or right to sue appears.
fable.s: for security and visitor safety activities related to the Presidential Inaugural Ceremonies, at a rate for operations of $2,000,000

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple appropriation provision that allocates funds for specific operational activities (security and visitor safety). It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before a decision is made. It merely authorizes spending.
qwen_block.s: In addition to the amounts otherwise provided by section 101, an additional amount is provided for “Department of the Interior—National Park Service—Operation of the National Park System” for security and visitor safety activities related to the Presidential Inaugural Ceremonies, at a rate for operations of $2,000,000.

opus.w: This section only adds $2,000,000 to National Park Service funding for security and visitor safety at the Presidential Inaugural Ceremonies. It doesn't set up any process that brings outside parties into a federal decision. A public event being mentioned isn't the same as public participation in decision-making, and nothing in the text is on-topic, so the quoted span is empty.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking.** The only possible pull toward "Yes" is the mention of "Presidential Inaugural Ceremonies," which are public events. That reading doesn't hold up. The section just gives the National Park Service extra money for security and visitor safety. It doesn't require or allow any consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue, so no one outside the federal government takes part in a federal decision.
